patch_description: Both prior programs plateau at combined_score 0.39, indicating the randomized jitter local search gets stuck in poor local optima. The crossover combines the faster random-search skeleton (program 1) with the bottleneck-targeted polish (program 2), and adds two key improvements: (1) structured symmetric seeds (near-uniform lattice arrangements known to be strong starting points for Heilbronn-type problems, e.g. hexagonal/perturbed-lattice placements), and (2) an aggressive "bottleneck relief" move that pushes all three vertices of the worst triangle away from its centroid, which escapes local optima that single-point jitter cannot. Multi-scale descent (coarse jitter → bottleneck polish → micro jitter) with fewer seeds keeps runtime near the faster variant while searching deeper. Deterministic seeds and the same fallback guarantee identical interface and robustness.
